Subject: Re: Quick demo follow-up + next steps

Thanks for the demo today — the team appreciated the walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can validate fit on our side before committing to a short pilot: 

- What we heard: 1) latency during peak trading-hours is the top non-negotiable (p95 target ~120ms on 1–2k token requests); 2) cost sensitivity over sustained usage (we expect steady-state token volume ~100M tokens/month in the pilot); 3) deterministic behavior on policy prompts is important (we need low regression risk as we iterate prompts).

- Asks: 
  * Can you share your recommended model shortlist with concrete cost/latency estimates and any known failure modes?
  * A test prompt set we can run against our internal evaluator (will include policy-check and risk prompts).
  * A suggested acceptance criteria matrix for the pilot (latency, semantic accuracy, regression tolerance).

We attached the internal test-plan (high level) to this thread. Our goal is to kick off a 4-week pilot in early July if validation looks clean.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Data Products
FinQuant

Subject: FinQuant POC — proposed model shortlist & validation plan

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and for flagging the p95 latency target. Per the demo and follow-up with our eng team, we ran a quick micro-benchmark on representative payloads and are proposing the following shortlist with tradeoffs and suggested acceptance thresholds. I focused on options that balance your latency requirement with cost predictability and minimal regression risk when applying prompt engineering.

Shortlist (ordered by recommendation):
1) redwood-throughput-8b (FP16) — Recommended baseline
   - Why: Excellent latency at 1–2k tokens due to attention kernel tuning; strong instruction-following for domain prompts after lightweight fine-tuning.
   - Benchmarks (median): p50=45ms, p95=120ms (on our 4xA100 reserved cluster, conservative estimates).
   - Cost: estimated $0.20 / 1k prompt tokens + $0.06 / 1k completion tokens (approx for reserved capacity pricing).
   - Risks: lower absolute ROUGE on very long-context recall items vs 13B models; low regression risk on policy prompts after prompt stabilization.

2) open-llama-34b-8bit (quantized) — Higher-quality option for semantics
   - Why: Substantially better long-context fidelity and fewer hallucinations on domain-specific numeric reasoning.
   - Benchmarks (median): p50=110ms, p95=260ms (we recommend dedicated capacity to meet p95 targets).
   - Cost: estimated $0.45 / 1k prompt tokens + $0.18 / 1k completion tokens (higher GPU footprint).
   - Risks: higher cost and more opportunity for latency spikes during bursty traffic. Requires our autoscaling + fallback policy for graceful degradation.

3) redwood-econ-13b-8bit — Middle ground for cost/quality
   - Why: Good semantic performance on financial language with lower cost than 34B; predictable latency with conservative batching.
   - Benchmarks (median): p50=70ms, p95=160ms.
   - Cost: estimated $0.30 / 1k prompt tokens + $0.09 / 1k completion tokens.
   - Risks: can show regressions on adversarial policy prompts if prompts change frequently — recommend running our regression suite during rollout.

Quality/regression notes and suggested controls:
- Regression tolerance: we recommend setting an initial guardrail of no more than a 5% drop in semantic-accuracy F1 across the provided prompt set (we'll share the comparator script). Anything beyond that should trigger a canary rollback.
- Prompt-set: attached prompt_set_regression_suite_v1.md — includes 120 curated prompts: 40 policy-sensitive, 40 numerical-extraction/regression checks, 40 conversational/context-drop tests.
- Eval harness: link to an evaluation notebook with example runs (see related_links). We'll run the first pass on our side, then provide a results snapshot for your team within 48 hours once you share access to the test harness and a sample of real traffic (anonymized).

Proposed acceptance criteria (starter matrix):
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms on 1–2k token requests OR automatic fallback to a lower-latency model that preserves semantic parity for high priority endpoints.
- Semantic accuracy: >= 92% on key extraction prompts (F1) and <= 5% relative regression vs baseline.
- Behavioral: 0 critical policy failures on policy-sensitive prompts in the regression suite.

Next steps we suggest: 
- You: share the anonymized sample request set + any regulatory prompts (Jared?) by June 4.
- Us (Redwood): provision a short-lived dev endpoint for the three shortlisted models and run the first-pass benchmark + regression suite by June 7.
- Joint: sync week of June 8 for results + decision on pilot scope (we can do a 30-min verification call).

Attachments included: finquant_poc_benchmarks_v1.csv, prompt_set_regression_suite_v1.md, FQ_mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf

If you want, we can also include a small canary run that instruments token-level cost tracking and early-fail checks for policy prompts.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
